locations.name: Pittman's Gas and Service
locations.description: Four pumps under a buzzing canopy where the state highway meets the river road, with a bus-stop sign bolted to the ice machine and a hand-lettered board out front that reads CRICKETS, NIGHT CRAWLERS, CARTONS. Out back, two open service bays smell of hot oil and tire rubber, and a radio plays gospel to whatever truck is up on the lift.

locations.name: The Low Water
locations.description: A cinderblock bar on Front Street with neon beer signs in the window, a pool table with a slow lean and a flood line drawn in marker beside the door. On weekends the gravel lot fills with car tags from the dry county, and the kitchen hatch at the back sends out catfish baskets and the smell of old fryer grease.

locations.name: The Riverview Motor Court
locations.description: Twelve rooms in a single-story L around a cracked parking lot, under a sign that says VACANCY in every season and a name that promises a view you only get from behind the dumpster. The office smells of burnt coffee and air freshener, and a monitor on the counter shows the lot in four gray squares.

locations.name: Riverside Baptist Church
locations.description: A white clapboard church on the slope above Front Street, with a steeple that leans a little toward the river and a marquee sign out front that reads PRAY FOR OUR BRIDGE. Inside, the pews smell of lemon polish and old hymnals, and the fellowship hall out back keeps a coffee urn and a box of donated coats going all week.

locations.name: Town Hall
locations.description: A two-story brick building with the mayor's office upstairs and the police department downstairs, one patrol car out front and a second up on blocks behind it. The station is a front counter, three desks and a single holding cell, and the window unit drips onto a box of unpaid parking tickets.

locations.name: Byrd's Pawn
locations.description: A narrow storefront between two empty ones, its window crowded with chainsaws, guitars and fishing reels behind a security grille that never goes all the way up. Inside it smells of gun oil and stale smoke, and a glass counter of rings and phones sits under a hand-lettered sign that says NO REFUNDS NO STORIES.

locations.name: Riverbend Trailer Park
locations.description: Thirty-odd trailers on the low ground downstream of the landing, some with flower boxes and some with blue tarps on the roofs, strung along a gravel loop that floods to the axles every spring. Dogs bark on chains, a trampoline rusts in the middle of the loop, and a cross of plastic flowers is wired to the fence by the mailboxes.

locations.name: Purvis Landing
locations.description: A bait shop on stilts, a fuel pump and a floating dock of aluminum johnboats and bass boats, beside the concrete public ramp where the river road runs straight down into the water. At night the dock lights stay off, and every morning the mud at the foot of the ramp is cut with fresh trailer tracks.

locations.name: Sturdivant House
locations.description: A white two-story house with eight columns on the hill above town, its lawn mowed in stripes and its paint peeling on the side nobody sees from the road. At the end of the drive by the water tower you can get the town's one bar of cell signal, and there is usually a truck parked there with someone holding a phone up to the sky.

locations.name: The Old Bridge
locations.description: A narrow green steel truss from 1938, two lanes and no shoulder, posted at five tons and rattling under every pickup that crosses toward the dry county. Halfway over, a sign on the rail marks the state line, and fishermen leave cut bait and beer cans on the concrete pier below the first span.

memories.text: bought me a beer at the bar

npcs.name: Loretta Gaddis
npcs.role: owner and bartender of the Low Water
npcs.look: Rail-thin woman of sixty with frosted hair, reading glasses on a beaded chain and a bar towel over one shoulder.
npcs.voice: Flat and unhurried; calls everybody 'hon', answers a question she doesn't like by asking what you're drinking, and never says a name out loud if she can point instead.
npcs.goal: Keep the old bridge open, because half her trade drives over from the dry county and none of it will drive the long way round.
npcs.secret: She has been seeing Royce Pittman on Tuesday afternoons for eleven years, and she is the reason he has not promised his vote to Carter Sturdivant.

memories.text: called me a liar in my own station

npcs.name: Royce Pittman
npcs.role: owner of Pittman's Gas and Service and the swing vote on the town council
npcs.look: Big, soft-bellied man in his fifties in a feed-store cap and a short-sleeved dress shirt, with a pen behind each ear.
npcs.voice: Folksy and slippery; dodges a straight answer, now and then with a story about his daddy; once in a while hedges with 'now, I'm not saying'; laughs to fill a silence.
npcs.goal: Get out from under the note on his station without having to pick a side where anybody can see him do it.
npcs.secret: Carter Sturdivant holds the note on the station and has offered to tear it up and give him the truck stop lease at the new interchange in return for a yes vote.

memories.text: helped carry the outboard motor down to the ramp

npcs.name: Vada Sturdivant
npcs.role: widow who owns Sturdivant House and the bottomland downstream
npcs.look: Small, straight-backed woman of eighty in a cardigan and pearls, with garden dirt under her nails and a cane she points with more than she leans on.
npcs.voice: Crisp and formal, with an old schoolteacher's diction; calls grown men 'son', corrects your grammar mid-sentence, and answers questions about money by asking who your people are.
npcs.goal: Keep the old bridge her father fought the state for in 1938, and keep the bottomland out of Carter's hands while she is alive.
npcs.secret: The Sturdivant money started with her father running whiskey into the dry county, and Wade Purvis still brings her an envelope every month, which is why the landing lease has never gone up.

memories.text: Loose end with Tester (a debt): I owe a man in this town more money than I can pay.
Tester let the six hundred go past due, so I took the phone as a start.
Tester let the six hundred go past due, so I took the phone as a start.

npcs.name: Carter Sturdivant
npcs.role: head of Sturdivant Land and Timber, who holds half the town's paper
npcs.look: Trim, tanned man of forty-five in a quarter-zip pullover and pressed khakis, turning a truck key fob over and over in his fingers.
npcs.voice: Fast and friendly, like a salesman closing; uses your first name too soon and too often, talks about 'the future of this town', and states every sum to the dollar.
npcs.goal: Get the new bridge built downstream on Sturdivant bottomland, sell the state the right-of-way and own the truck stop at the new interchange.
npcs.secret: He is two years behind on the family's timber loans, and he has asked a doctor in the city to find his mother Vada unfit so he can sign the bottomland over himself.

memories.text: kept quiet about what I told them and stood up for me

npcs.name: Jolene Overstreet
npcs.role: mayor and town clerk
npcs.look: Heavy-set woman in her fifties in a cardigan over a church T-shirt, with a lanyard of keys and a phone she keeps checking for a signal it never finds.
npcs.voice: Brisk and procedural; cites ordinances by number, says 'that's a council matter' to shut a subject, and drops to a whisper to say anything kind.
npcs.goal: Get the downstream bridge approved and the police department dissolved before the town's money runs out in January.
npcs.secret: Carter Sturdivant pays her five hundred dollars a month in cash, handed over in the motel parking lot, and she used the first year of it to cover money missing from the water fund.

npcs.name: Hollis Byrd
npcs.role: owner of Byrd's Pawn
npcs.look: Stooped, pot-bellied man of sixty-five in suspenders and a fishing vest, with a jeweler's loupe on a cord and a toothpick that never leaves his mouth.
npcs.voice: Slow and sideways, never a straight yes or no; calls everything 'merchandise', prices things before you ask, and says 'I don't ask where, I ask how much.'
npcs.goal: Sell the shop and retire to the coast before the bridge closes and the building is worth nothing.
npcs.secret: He runs the Night Run's cash through his books as pawn sales, and the catalytic converters stacked behind the shop came off cars in three counties.

npcs.name: Wade Purvis
npcs.role: owner of Purvis Landing and boss of the Night Run
npcs.look: Lean, sunburnt man in his fifties with a gray ponytail, a faded camouflage cap and the tip of one finger missing.
npcs.voice: Quiet and dry; lets you talk yourself out, answers in river terms like stage, chop and slack water, and never says the word police, only 'the law'.
npcs.goal: Keep the old bridge open and the river unwatched after dark, and keep his nephew out of prison.
npcs.secret: He knows Colt is selling pills on the side and has not stopped him, because Colt was there the night Wade beat a man half to death for cutting in on the run, and could send him to prison for it.

npcs.name: Colt Purvis
npcs.role: deckhand on the Night Run
npcs.look: Wiry kid of twenty-two in a sleeveless shirt and white rubber boots, with a fresh tattoo still peeling on his forearm.
npcs.voice: Fast and jumpy; talks over you, calls men 'bro' and women 'ma'am', brags about money he doesn't have, and laughs at things that aren't funny.
npcs.goal: Make enough money to quit working for his uncle and buy a truck in his own name.
npcs.secret: He sells pain pills bought across the river to people at Riverbend, and the bottle Amber Lott died with came from him.

npcs.name: Marcus Bell
npcs.role: chief of police
npcs.look: Tall, heavy-shouldered man of fifty in a pressed uniform shirt gone tight at the buttons, with a shaved head and a limp he hides badly.
npcs.voice: Courteous and relentless; says 'sir' and 'ma'am', asks the same question three different ways, and writes your answers in a pocket notebook while you watch him do it.
npcs.goal: Make a bust big enough to save his department before the council votes to dissolve it, and prove the bridge report was bought.
npcs.secret: He has known for months that Travis Cagle takes Night Run money and has let it go on, because he needs Travis on the payroll until the vote and on the witness stand after it.

npcs.name: Travis Cagle
npcs.role: night-shift police officer
npcs.look: Thick-necked man of twenty-eight in a uniform with the sleeves rolled, a dip of tobacco in his lip and a new watch too nice for his pay.
npcs.voice: Loud and buddy-buddy, all 'my man' and 'hoss'; talks about his boat, laughs before his own punchlines, and goes quiet the second anyone mentions money.
npcs.goal: Keep taking Wade Purvis's money until his boat is paid off, then get on with the county before anyone looks closely.
npcs.secret: Wade Purvis pays him three hundred dollars a week to park at the motel during the runs, and he keeps Wade's texts on a second phone in case he ever needs to trade them.

npcs.name: Ray Dees
npcs.role: pastor of Riverside Baptist Church
npcs.look: Round-faced man of sixty-five in a short-sleeved white shirt and clip-on tie, with a hearing aid and a pocket full of peppermints.
npcs.voice: Slow and warm, with a preacher's rhythm even at the gas pump; sometimes answers a hard question with a Bible story, and somehow gets the answer out of you instead.
npcs.goal: Keep the Riverbend families housed and fed through the winter, and bury no more young people this year.
npcs.secret: The church's new roof was paid for by an anonymous cash gift that he knows came from Wade Purvis, and he has preached against the Night Run every Sunday since without giving a dollar of it back.

npcs.name: June Satterfield
npcs.role: retired nurse who patches people up at her kitchen table
npcs.look: Stout woman of sixty in scrub pants and a sweatshirt from a hospital that closed, with her gray hair in a clip and a canvas bag that rattles.
npcs.voice: Blunt and clinical; asks what you took and how much before she asks your name, swears mildly, and never tells anyone not to worry.
npcs.goal: Keep Riverbend's people out of an emergency room forty miles away, and get the pills off the lot without anyone she knows going to prison.
npcs.secret: She has reversed four overdoses at Riverbend this fall without reporting one, and three of the four told her they bought from Colt Purvis.

npcs.name: Dewayne Mangum
npcs.role: mechanic in the service bays at Pittman's
npcs.look: Short, broad man of forty with grease worked into every knuckle, safety glasses pushed up on a bald head and a shop rag in his back pocket.
npcs.voice: Few words, all of them about engines; says 'mm-hm' for yes and 'well' for no, and talks to the truck he's working on more than to you.
npcs.goal: Save enough to buy the empty garage on Front Street and stop working out of Royce Pittman's bays.
npcs.secret: On the morning of the bridge inspection he towed the engineer's rental car out of a ditch and watched Carter Sturdivant drive the man off to lunch, though the report says he spent the whole day under the spans.

memories.text: Loose end with Tester (a secret): Someone here knows what I did before I came.

npcs.name: Tyler Rasberry
npcs.role: night clerk at the Riverview Motor Court
npcs.look: Gangly young man of nineteen with a patchy beard, a gaming headset round his neck and a phone with a cracked screen always in his hand.
npcs.voice: Mumbles and deflects with internet jokes and never meets your eye, then turns precise the moment cash is on the counter: plates, times, room numbers.
npcs.goal: Save enough cash to leave Lockett's Ferry for good and never work another night shift.
npcs.secret: The motel's parking-lot camera has caught Carter Sturdivant handing Jolene Overstreet an envelope every month since spring, and Tyler has copied the clips to a thumb drive he is trying to sell.

npcs.name: Tammy Lott
npcs.role: cook at the Low Water
npcs.look: Hollow-eyed woman of forty-two in a hairnet and a stained Low Water T-shirt, with her daughter's name tattooed fresh on the inside of her wrist.
npcs.voice: Hoarse and short; says exactly what she thinks in as few words as possible, swears at the grill, and goes very calm and polite when she is angriest.
npcs.goal: See whoever sold Amber the pills that killed her locked up or run out of town.
npcs.secret: She took a tire iron to Colt Purvis's truck the week after the funeral, and Wade Purvis paid for the windshield himself and told her the next one would cost her more.

npcs.name: Odell Gandy
npcs.role: old enemy
npcs.look: Big, quiet man in a pressed denim shirt, with a healed scar through one eyebrow and knuckles like walnuts.
npcs.voice: Says very little, all of it polite, and always uses your full name.
npcs.goal: Settle an old score with the newcomer, quietly and for good.
npcs.secret: He has already spent the money he was paid to find the newcomer, so he cannot go home until it is done.

factions.name: Sturdivant Land and Timber
factions.goal: Get the old bridge closed and the new state bridge built five miles downstream on Sturdivant bottomland, then sell the state the right-of-way and put a truck stop at the new interchange.
factions.methods: Private loans and contracts for deed that can be called in on a week's notice, a mayor paid in cash, a bridge report bought from a consulting engineer, and a lawyer in the city.

onComplete.text: Royce Pittman votes with the mayor, the council backs the downstream bridge site three to two, and the state puts the old bridge on its closure list.

rumour.text: The council voted three to two for the downstream bridge, and Royce Pittman was the third vote.

onComplete.text: Carter Sturdivant refuses to renew the lease on Purvis Landing, a lawyer's notice goes up on the bait shop door, and Wade Purvis starts putting his boats in off the bank at Riverbend after dark.

seed.cause: Vada Sturdivant has found out that Carter pulled the Purvis Landing lease, which ends an arrangement with Wade Purvis that she has never told her son about.
seed.effect: Vada Sturdivant, white with anger at her son, asks whoever is in front of her to carry a sealed envelope down to Wade Purvis and put it in his hand and nobody else's.

rumour.text: Carter Sturdivant pulled the lease on Purvis Landing, and Wade Purvis is putting his boats in off the bank at Riverbend now.

onComplete.text: A state crew sets concrete barriers across both ends of the old bridge, and every trip to the dry county is now forty minutes round by the highway.

rumour.text: The state has put concrete barriers across the old bridge, and the drive to the dry county is forty minutes round by the highway now.

factions.name: The Town Police
factions.goal: Make an arrest big enough to save the department before the council votes to dissolve it, and prove that the bridge report was bought.
factions.methods: Traffic stops at the bridge approach, a motel clerk paid twenty dollars a tip, sitting dark above the boat ramp, and leaning on anyone with an open warrant.

clocks.label: Catch a boat at the ramp

onComplete.text: Chief Bell catches Colt Purvis at the foot of the ramp at three in the morning with a johnboat full of cartons and a pocket full of pills, and the Night Run pulls its boats up on the bank.

rumour.text: Chief Bell caught Colt Purvis at the ramp with a boat full of cartons and a pocket full of pills.

onComplete.text: Chief Bell arrests Hollis Byrd over a stack of stolen catalytic converters behind the shop, and by morning Hollis is talking about whose cash goes through his books.

seed.cause: Hollis Byrd, in the holding cell, wants to trade what he knows about the Night Run's money before Wade Purvis hears he is talking.
seed.effect: From the holding cell, Hollis Byrd calls out to anyone who comes into the station that he will say where the Night Run keeps its cash if they get word to his daughter in the city first.

rumour.text: Hollis Byrd is in the holding cell over a stack of stolen catalytic converters, and they say he is talking.

onComplete.text: Chief Bell lays the motel camera footage and the engineer's lunch receipt in front of the council, and the state police take Jolene Overstreet out of Town Hall in handcuffs.

rumour.text: The state police walked Jolene Overstreet out of Town Hall in handcuffs, and it was over the bridge report.

factions.name: The Night Run
factions.goal: Keep the old bridge open and the river unwatched after dark, so cartons and cases keep crossing into the dry county the way they have for sixty years.
factions.methods: Johnboats with no running lights, pickups kept under the weight limit, cash to the night-shift officer, and photographs of anyone who votes the wrong way.

onComplete.text: Travis Cagle stops patrolling after midnight altogether, the boats cross every night, and Wade Purvis is buying every carton and case Pittman's can order.

rumour.text: Nobody patrols after midnight any more, and Wade Purvis is buying every carton and case Pittman's can order.

onComplete.text: Somebody leaves photographs of Royce Pittman and Loretta Gaddis on the seat of Royce's truck, and the next day he takes back his support for the downstream bridge and asks for a new vote.

rumour.text: Somebody left photographs of Royce Pittman and Loretta Gaddis in his truck, and now he wants a new vote on the bridge.

onComplete.text: After an anonymous call, the county sheriff finds three cartons and a bottle of pills under the seat of Chief Bell's truck, and the mayor suspends him and he leaves to stay with his sister in the city.

seed.cause: Travis Cagle knows the Night Run made the call that ended Chief Bell, and he is afraid of what Wade Purvis will ask of him next.
seed.effect: Travis Cagle, acting chief now and sweating through his shirt, asks to talk somewhere private and wants someone outside the department to keep his second phone, the one with Wade Purvis's texts on it.

rumour.text: The county sheriff found cartons and pills under the seat of Chief Bell's truck, and the mayor suspended him the same night.

threads.title: The bridge vote
threads.summary: The state has rated the old bridge critical and will pay for one new crossing, either in town or five miles downstream on Sturdivant bottomland. The council votes on the site this month, and Royce Pittman is the one vote nobody can count.

threads.title: Disbanding the police
threads.summary: Mayor Jolene Overstreet wants to dissolve the three-officer police department and pay the county sheriff to patrol the town instead. Chief Bell has until the budget meeting to show the council what his department is worth.

rumours.text: The engineer who condemned the bridge spent inspection day eating catfish at the Low Water with Carter Sturdivant, not under the spans.
The mayor meets Carter Sturdivant in the motel parking lot once a month after dark, and she never goes inside.
Travis Cagle paid cash for a new bass boat this summer, and nobody buys a boat like that on a night-shift salary.
The pills at Riverbend come from Colt Purvis, and his uncle Wade either does not know or does not want to.
Royce Pittman owes the Sturdivants on the station, which is why he still will not say how he will vote.
Miss Vada will not sign the bottomland over for the new bridge, and Carter cannot sell it without her.
The mayor wants to get rid of the police and hand the town to the county sheriff before Christmas.
Something in the deep hole under the old bridge pulls a swimmer down every seven years, and this is the seventh year.
Loretta Gaddis has already sold the Low Water to the Sturdivants and is only waiting for the bridge to close to tell anyone.
June Satterfield lost her nursing license for stealing pills from the hospital, and that is where the Riverbend pills come from.

town.name: Lockett's Ferry
town.setting: Lockett's Ferry is a river town of about eight hundred people where the state highway drops off the bluff and crosses the Lusk River on a narrow green steel bridge built in 1938. The state line runs down the middle of the river, the county on the far side is dry and taxes cigarettes hard, and for as long as anyone can remember, cartons and cases have gone across at night, by johnboat from Purvis Landing or in pickups light enough for the bridge's five-ton limit. Now the state has rated the bridge critical and will pay for one new crossing, either here or five miles downstream on Sturdivant land, and the town council votes on the site this month. Carter Sturdivant wants it downstream, the Night Run wants the old bridge open and the river dark, and the three-officer police department needs an arrest big enough to stop the mayor disbanding it. Cell signal is patchy in the valley, one bar if you stand by the water tower on the hill, so business here is done face to face: at the bar, at the pumps, at the ramp. People tell stories about what the river takes, but nobody you would believe has ever seen anything in it but mud and catfish.

Out back, two open service bays smell of hot oil and tire rubber, and a radio plays gospel to whatever truck is up on the lift.

locations.name: The Low Water
locations.description: A cinderblock bar on Front Street with neon beer signs in the window, a pool table with a slow lean and a flood line drawn in marker beside the door. On weekends the gravel lot fills with car tags from the dry county, and the kitchen hatch at the back sends out catfish baskets and the smell of old fryer grease.

locations.name: The Riverview Motor Court
locations.description: Twelve rooms in a single-story L around a cracked parking lot, under a sign that says VACANCY in every season and a name that promises a view you only get from behind the dumpster. The office smells of burnt coffee and air freshener, and a monitor on the counter shows the lot in four gray squares.

locations.name: Riverside Baptist Church
locations.description: A white clapboard church on the slope above Front Street, with a steeple that leans a little toward the river and a marquee sign out front that reads PRAY FOR OUR BRIDGE. Inside, the pews smell of lemon polish and old hymnals, and the fellowship hall out back keeps a coffee urn and a box of donated coats going all week.

locations.name: Town Hall
locations.description: A two-story brick building with the mayor's office upstairs and the police department downstairs, one patrol car out front and a second up on blocks behind it. The station is a front counter, three desks and a single holding cell, and the window unit drips onto a box of unpaid parking tickets.

locations.name: Byrd's Pawn
locations.description: A narrow storefront between two empty ones, its window crowded with chainsaws, guitars and fishing reels behind a security grille that never goes all the way up. Inside it smells of gun oil and stale smoke, and a glass counter of rings and phones sits under a hand-lettered sign that says NO REFUNDS NO STORIES.

locations.name: Riverbend Trailer Park
locations.description: Thirty-odd trailers on the low ground downstream of the landing, some with flower boxes and some with blue tarps on the roofs, strung along a gravel loop that floods to the axles every spring. Dogs bark on chains, a trampoline rusts in the middle of the loop, and a cross of plastic flowers is wired to the fence by the mailboxes.

locations.name: Purvis Landing
locations.description: A bait shop on stilts, a fuel pump and a floating dock of aluminum johnboats and bass boats, beside the concrete public ramp where the river road runs straight down into the water. At night the dock lights stay off, and every morning the mud at the foot of the ramp is cut with fresh trailer tracks.

locations.name: Sturdivant House
locations.description: A white two-story house with eight columns on the hill above town, its lawn mowed in stripes and its paint peeling on the side nobody sees from the road. At the end of the drive by the water tower you can get the town's one bar of cell signal, and there is usually a truck parked there with someone holding a phone up to the sky.

locations.name: The Old Bridge
locations.description: A narrow green steel truss from 1938, two lanes and no shoulder, posted at five tons and rattling under every pickup that crosses toward the dry county. Halfway over, a sign on the rail marks the state line, and fishermen leave cut bait and beer cans on the concrete pier below the first span.

npcs.name: Loretta Gaddis
npcs.role: owner and bartender of the Low Water
npcs.look: Rail-thin woman of sixty with frosted hair, reading glasses on a beaded chain and a bar towel over one shoulder.
npcs.voice: Flat and unhurried; calls everybody 'hon', answers a question she doesn't like by asking what you're drinking, and never says a name out loud if she can point instead.
npcs.goal: Keep the old bridge open, because half her trade drives over from the dry county and none of it will drive the long way round.
npcs.secret: She has been seeing Royce Pittman on Tuesday afternoons for eleven years, and she is the reason he has not promised his vote to Carter Sturdivant.

npcs.name: Royce Pittman
npcs.role: owner of Pittman's Gas and Service and the swing vote on the town council
npcs.look: Big, soft-bellied man in his fifties in a feed-store cap and a short-sleeved dress shirt, with a pen behind each ear.
npcs.voice: Folksy and slippery; dodges a straight answer, now and then with a story about his daddy; once in a while hedges with 'now, I'm not saying'; laughs to fill a silence.
npcs.goal: Get out from under the note on his station without having to pick a side where anybody can see him do it.
npcs.secret: Carter Sturdivant holds the note on the station and has offered to tear it up and give him the truck stop lease at the new interchange in return for a yes vote.

npcs.name: Vada Sturdivant
npcs.role: widow who owns Sturdivant House and the bottomland downstream
npcs.look: Small, straight-backed woman of eighty in a cardigan and pearls, with garden dirt under her nails and a cane she points with more than she leans on.
npcs.voice: Crisp and formal, with an old schoolteacher's diction; calls grown men 'son', corrects your grammar mid-sentence, and answers questions about money by asking who your people are.
npcs.goal: Keep the old bridge her father fought the state for in 1938, and keep the bottomland out of Carter's hands while she is alive.
npcs.secret: The Sturdivant money started with her father running whiskey into the dry county, and Wade Purvis still brings her an envelope every month, which is why the landing lease has never gone up.

npcs.name: Carter Sturdivant
npcs.role: head of Sturdivant Land and Timber, who holds half the town's paper
npcs.look: Trim, tanned man of forty-five in a quarter-zip pullover and pressed khakis, turning a truck key fob over and over in his fingers.
npcs.voice: Fast and friendly, like a salesman closing; uses your first name too soon and too often, talks about 'the future of this town', and states every sum to the dollar.
npcs.goal: Get the new bridge built downstream on Sturdivant bottomland, sell the state the right-of-way and own the truck stop at the new interchange.
npcs.secret: He is two years behind on the family's timber loans, and he has asked a doctor in the city to find his mother Vada unfit so he can sign the bottomland over himself.

npcs.name: Jolene Overstreet
npcs.role: mayor and town clerk
npcs.look: Heavy-set woman in her fifties in a cardigan over a church T-shirt, with a lanyard of keys and a phone she keeps checking for a signal it never finds.
npcs.voice: Brisk and procedural; cites ordinances by number, says 'that's a council matter' to shut a subject, and drops to a whisper to say anything kind.
npcs.goal: Get the downstream bridge approved and the police department dissolved before the town's money runs out in January.
npcs.secret: Carter Sturdivant pays her five hundred dollars a month in cash, handed over in the motel parking lot, and she used the first year of it to cover money missing from the water fund.

npcs.name: Hollis Byrd
npcs.role: owner of Byrd's Pawn
npcs.look: Stooped, pot-bellied man of sixty-five in suspenders and a fishing vest, with a jeweler's loupe on a cord and a toothpick that never leaves his mouth.
npcs.voice: Slow and sideways, never a straight yes or no; calls everything 'merchandise', prices things before you ask, and says 'I don't ask where, I ask how much.'
npcs.goal: Sell the shop and retire to the coast before the bridge closes and the building is worth nothing.
npcs.secret: He runs the Night Run's cash through his books as pawn sales, and the catalytic converters stacked behind the shop came off cars in three counties.

npcs.name: Wade Purvis
npcs.role: owner of Purvis Landing and boss of the Night Run
npcs.look: Lean, sunburnt man in his fifties with a gray ponytail, a faded camouflage cap and the tip of one finger missing.
npcs.voice: Quiet and dry; lets you talk yourself out, answers in river terms like stage, chop and slack water, and never says the word police, only 'the law'.
npcs.goal: Keep the old bridge open and the river unwatched after dark, and keep his nephew out of prison.
npcs.secret: He knows Colt is selling pills on the side and has not stopped him, because Colt was there the night Wade beat a man half to death for cutting in on the run, and could send him to prison for it.

npcs.name: Colt Purvis
npcs.role: deckhand on the Night Run
npcs.look: Wiry kid of twenty-two in a sleeveless shirt and white rubber boots, with a fresh tattoo still peeling on his forearm.
npcs.voice: Fast and jumpy; talks over you, calls men 'bro' and women 'ma'am', brags about money he doesn't have, and laughs at things that aren't funny.
npcs.goal: Make enough money to quit working for his uncle and buy a truck in his own name.
npcs.secret: He sells pain pills bought across the river to people at Riverbend, and the bottle Amber Lott died with came from him.

npcs.name: Marcus Bell
npcs.role: chief of police
npcs.look: Tall, heavy-shouldered man of fifty in a pressed uniform shirt gone tight at the buttons, with a shaved head and a limp he hides badly.
npcs.voice: Courteous and relentless; says 'sir' and 'ma'am', asks the same question three different ways, and writes your answers in a pocket notebook while you watch him do it.
npcs.goal: Make a bust big enough to save his department before the council votes to dissolve it, and prove the bridge report was bought.
npcs.secret: He has known for months that Travis Cagle takes Night Run money and has let it go on, because he needs Travis on the payroll until the vote and on the witness stand after it.

npcs.name: Travis Cagle
npcs.role: night-shift police officer
npcs.look: Thick-necked man of twenty-eight in a uniform with the sleeves rolled, a dip of tobacco in his lip and a new watch too nice for his pay.
npcs.voice: Loud and buddy-buddy, all 'my man' and 'hoss'; talks about his boat, laughs before his own punchlines, and goes quiet the second anyone mentions money.
npcs.goal: Keep taking Wade Purvis's money until his boat is paid off, then get on with the county before anyone looks closely.
npcs.secret: Wade Purvis pays him three hundred dollars a week to park at the motel during the runs, and he keeps Wade's texts on a second phone in case he ever needs to trade them.

npcs.name: Ray Dees
npcs.role: pastor of Riverside Baptist Church
npcs.look: Round-faced man of sixty-five in a short-sleeved white shirt and clip-on tie, with a hearing aid and a pocket full of peppermints.
npcs.voice: Slow and warm, with a preacher's rhythm even at the gas pump; sometimes answers a hard question with a Bible story, and somehow gets the answer out of you instead.
npcs.goal: Keep the Riverbend families housed and fed through the winter, and bury no more young people this year.
npcs.secret: The church's new roof was paid for by an anonymous cash gift that he knows came from Wade Purvis, and he has preached against the Night Run every Sunday since without giving a dollar of it back.

npcs.name: June Satterfield
npcs.role: retired nurse who patches people up at her kitchen table
npcs.look: Stout woman of sixty in scrub pants and a sweatshirt from a hospital that closed, with her gray hair in a clip and a canvas bag that rattles.
npcs.voice: Blunt and clinical; asks what you took and how much before she asks your name, swears mildly, and never tells anyone not to worry.
npcs.goal: Keep Riverbend's people out of an emergency room forty miles away, and get the pills off the lot without anyone she knows going to prison.
npcs.secret: She has reversed four overdoses at Riverbend this fall without reporting one, and three of the four told her they bought from Colt Purvis.

npcs.name: Dewayne Mangum
npcs.role: mechanic in the service bays at Pittman's
npcs.look: Short, broad man of forty with grease worked into every knuckle, safety glasses pushed up on a bald head and a shop rag in his back pocket.
npcs.voice: Few words, all of them about engines; says 'mm-hm' for yes and 'well' for no, and talks to the truck he's working on more than to you.
npcs.goal: Save enough to buy the empty garage on Front Street and stop working out of Royce Pittman's bays.
npcs.secret: On the morning of the bridge inspection he towed the engineer's rental car out of a ditch and watched Carter Sturdivant drive the man off to lunch, though the report says he spent the whole day under the spans.

npcs.name: Tyler Rasberry
npcs.role: night clerk at the Riverview Motor Court
npcs.look: Gangly young man of nineteen with a patchy beard, a gaming headset round his neck and a phone with a cracked screen always in his hand.
npcs.voice: Mumbles and deflects with internet jokes and never meets your eye, then turns precise the moment cash is on the counter: plates, times, room numbers.
npcs.goal: Save enough cash to leave Lockett's Ferry for good and never work another night shift.
npcs.secret: The motel's parking-lot camera has caught Carter Sturdivant handing Jolene Overstreet an envelope every month since spring, and Tyler has copied the clips to a thumb drive he is trying to sell.

npcs.name: Tammy Lott
npcs.role: cook at the Low Water
npcs.look: Hollow-eyed woman of forty-two in a hairnet and a stained Low Water T-shirt, with her daughter's name tattooed fresh on the inside of her wrist.
npcs.voice: Hoarse and short; says exactly what she thinks in as few words as possible, swears at the grill, and goes very calm and polite when she is angriest.
npcs.goal: See whoever sold Amber the pills that killed her locked up or run out of town.
npcs.secret: She took a tire iron to Colt Purvis's truck the week after the funeral, and Wade Purvis paid for the windshield himself and told her the next one would cost her more.

factions.name: Sturdivant Land and Timber
factions.goal: Get the old bridge closed and the new state bridge built five miles downstream on Sturdivant bottomland, then sell the state the right-of-way and put a truck stop at the new interchange.
factions.methods: Private loans and contracts for deed that can be called in on a week's notice, a mayor paid in cash, a bridge report bought from a consulting engineer, and a lawyer in the city.

onComplete.text: Royce Pittman votes with the mayor, the council backs the downstream bridge site three to two, and the state puts the old bridge on its closure list.

rumour.text: The council voted three to two for the downstream bridge, and Royce Pittman was the third vote.

onComplete.text: Carter Sturdivant refuses to renew the lease on Purvis Landing, a lawyer's notice goes up on the bait shop door, and Wade Purvis starts putting his boats in off the bank at Riverbend after dark.

seed.cause: Vada Sturdivant has found out that Carter pulled the Purvis Landing lease, which ends an arrangement with Wade Purvis that she has never told her son about.
seed.effect: Vada Sturdivant, white with anger at her son, asks whoever is in front of her to carry a sealed envelope down to Wade Purvis and put it in his hand and nobody else's.

rumour.text: Carter Sturdivant pulled the lease on Purvis Landing, and Wade Purvis is putting his boats in off the bank at Riverbend now.

onComplete.text: A state crew sets concrete barriers across both ends of the old bridge, and every trip to the dry county is now forty minutes round by the highway.

rumour.text: The state has put concrete barriers across the old bridge, and the drive to the dry county is forty minutes round by the highway now.

factions.name: The Town Police
factions.goal: Make an arrest big enough to save the department before the council votes to dissolve it, and prove that the bridge report was bought.
factions.methods: Traffic stops at the bridge approach, a motel clerk paid twenty dollars a tip, sitting dark above the boat ramp, and leaning on anyone with an open warrant.

clocks.label: Catch a boat at the ramp

onComplete.text: Chief Bell catches Colt Purvis at the foot of the ramp at three in the morning with a johnboat full of cartons and a pocket full of pills, and the Night Run pulls its boats up on the bank.

rumour.text: Chief Bell caught Colt Purvis at the ramp with a boat full of cartons and a pocket full of pills.

onComplete.text: Chief Bell arrests Hollis Byrd over a stack of stolen catalytic converters behind the shop, and by morning Hollis is talking about whose cash goes through his books.

seed.cause: Hollis Byrd, in the holding cell, wants to trade what he knows about the Night Run's money before Wade Purvis hears he is talking.
seed.effect: From the holding cell, Hollis Byrd calls out to anyone who comes into the station that he will say where the Night Run keeps its cash if they get word to his daughter in the city first.

rumour.text: Hollis Byrd is in the holding cell over a stack of stolen catalytic converters, and they say he is talking.

onComplete.text: Chief Bell lays the motel camera footage and the engineer's lunch receipt in front of the council, and the state police take Jolene Overstreet out of Town Hall in handcuffs.

rumour.text: The state police walked Jolene Overstreet out of Town Hall in handcuffs, and it was over the bridge report.

factions.name: The Night Run
factions.goal: Keep the old bridge open and the river unwatched after dark, so cartons and cases keep crossing into the dry county the way they have for sixty years.
factions.methods: Johnboats with no running lights, pickups kept under the weight limit, cash to the night-shift officer, and photographs of anyone who votes the wrong way.

onComplete.text: Travis Cagle stops patrolling after midnight altogether, the boats cross every night, and Wade Purvis is buying every carton and case Pittman's can order.

rumour.text: Nobody patrols after midnight any more, and Wade Purvis is buying every carton and case Pittman's can order.

onComplete.text: Somebody leaves photographs of Royce Pittman and Loretta Gaddis on the seat of Royce's truck, and the next day he takes back his support for the downstream bridge and asks for a new vote.

rumour.text: Somebody left photographs of Royce Pittman and Loretta Gaddis in his truck, and now he wants a new vote on the bridge.

onComplete.text: After an anonymous call, the county sheriff finds three cartons and a bottle of pills under the seat of Chief Bell's truck, and the mayor suspends him and he leaves to stay with his sister in the city.

seed.cause: Travis Cagle knows the Night Run made the call that ended Chief Bell, and he is afraid of what Wade Purvis will ask of him next.
seed.effect: Travis Cagle, acting chief now and sweating through his shirt, asks to talk somewhere private and wants someone outside the department to keep his second phone, the one with Wade Purvis's texts on it.

rumour.text: The county sheriff found cartons and pills under the seat of Chief Bell's truck, and the mayor suspended him the same night.

threads.title: The bridge vote
threads.summary: The state has rated the old bridge critical and will pay for one new crossing, either in town or five miles downstream on Sturdivant bottomland. The council votes on the site this month, and Royce Pittman is the one vote nobody can count.

threads.title: Disbanding the police
threads.summary: Mayor Jolene Overstreet wants to dissolve the three-officer police department and pay the county sheriff to patrol the town instead. Chief Bell has until the budget meeting to show the council what his department is worth.

threads.title: Pills at Riverbend
threads.summary: Two people at Riverbend have overdosed on pain pills since August, and one of them, nineteen-year-old Amber Lott, died. The chief says the pills come across the river; her mother says everybody knows who sells them.

seeds.cause: Wade Purvis has bought two hundred cartons and forty cases of liquor for the biggest run of the fall, and paid Travis Cagle to sit in the motel lot all night.
seeds.effect: The Night Run took a full load across the river overnight; Chief Bell is down at Purvis Landing photographing fresh trailer tracks on the ramp, and Wade Purvis is watching him from the bait shop with a cup of coffee.

seeds.cause: Carter Sturdivant has had a lawyer in the city write to Wade Purvis that the Purvis Landing lease will not be renewed at the new year.
seeds.effect: Wade Purvis read the lawyer's letter out loud at the Low Water last night and told Carter Sturdivant, in front of the whole bar, that the Sturdivants made their money on the same river.

seeds.cause: Jolene Overstreet has put the police budget on the next council agenda without telling Chief Bell.
seeds.effect: A typed agenda taped to the Town Hall door lists the dissolution of the police department as item four, and Chief Bell has been seen standing in front of it with his notebook out.

seeds.cause: Colt Purvis has a new bottle of pills from across the river and is selling them at Riverbend for less than before.
seeds.effect: June Satterfield brought a boy at Riverbend back from an overdose last night with the nasal spray she keeps in her purse and did not call it in; Tammy Lott is telling everyone at the Low Water that the pills were Colt Purvis's.

seeds.cause: The consulting engineer who wrote the bridge report has been asked to answer questions at the council meeting, and Carter Sturdivant does not want him answering any.
seeds.effect: The engineer canceled his appearance at the council meeting by email, and Dewayne Mangum told the counter at Pittman's that he towed that man's rental car out of a ditch on the morning of the inspection.

seeds.cause: Carter Sturdivant has asked a doctor in the city to find his mother unfit, so that he can sign the bottomland over to the state himself.
seeds.effect: Carter brought a doctor up to Sturdivant House yesterday, and Vada Sturdivant threw them both out and drove herself to Riverside Baptist to ask Pastor Dees to witness a new will.

seeds.cause: Colt Purvis keeps his pills and his sales phone in a tackle box wedged on a girder under the first span of the old bridge, where his uncle never looks.
seeds.effect: On a girder ledge under the first span, reachable from the riverbank, is a tackle box holding three pill bottles with a pharmacy label from across the river and a cheap prepaid phone full of texts from Riverbend numbers.

rumours.text: The engineer who condemned the bridge spent inspection day eating catfish at the Low Water with Carter Sturdivant, not under the spans.
The mayor meets Carter Sturdivant in the motel parking lot once a month after dark, and she never goes inside.
Travis Cagle paid cash for a new bass boat this summer, and nobody buys a boat like that on a night-shift salary.
The pills at Riverbend come from Colt Purvis, and his uncle Wade either does not know or does not want to.
Royce Pittman owes the Sturdivants on the station, which is why he still will not say how he will vote.
Miss Vada will not sign the bottomland over for the new bridge, and Carter cannot sell it without her.
The mayor wants to get rid of the police and hand the town to the county sheriff before Christmas.
Something in the deep hole under the old bridge pulls a swimmer down every seven years, and this is the seventh year.
Loretta Gaddis has already sold the Low Water to the Sturdivants and is only waiting for the bridge to close to tell anyone.
June Satterfield lost her nursing license for stealing pills from the hospital, and that is where the Riverbend pills come from.
